Background (from the session that started this one):
Maester 3.0 is moving every shared tenant value to a test parameter bound to a registered setting (`[MaesterParameter(Setting = '...')]`), designed in issue 2775 and implemented in PR 2758 (branch `feat/parameter-settings`). That PR registered `ParkedDomains` (`string[]`, kind `Entra.Domain`) in `powershell/assets/MaesterSettings.psd1` but left the CISA Exchange tests inferring parked domains from Exchange's `SendingFromDomainDisabled`. The owner (Merill) has decided those tests should use `ParkedDomains` too, in a separate PR because it changes their results. The CIS equivalents are handled in PR 2673 and must be left alone.

Task:
In the Maester repo (read `AGENTS.md` first), switch the CISA Exchange email-authentication tests from inferring parked domains to the shared `ParkedDomains` setting, and open a PR.

Today the tests under `tests/cisa/exchange/` that check SPF, DKIM and DMARC (find them by searching `tests/cisa` for `SendingFromDomainDisabled`, `Force`/`AllDomains`, and the SPF/DKIM/DMARC helpers; CISA EXO 2.x and 4.x are the likely ones) decide which accepted domains are parked from the Exchange property `SendingFromDomainDisabled`. Change them so that a domain is parked when it is listed in a parameter bound to the setting:

```powershell
# Domains that never send email.
[MaesterParameter(Setting = 'ParkedDomains')]
[string[]] $ParkedDomains = @()
```

Rules:
- A test never calls `Get-MtSetting` for this; the engine binds the parameter (precedence: `-Parameter`, the test's `TestSettings` row, `GlobalSettings`, the default). See "Values set once for many tests" in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx` and "Parameter names" / "Parameters bound to a setting" in `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md`.
- Before changing each test, read what SCuBA asks for that policy (the requirement in `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json`, the test's `.md`, and the ScubaGear baseline text for MS.EXO.2.x/4.x) and say in the PR what a parked domain must publish for each policy, so the new behaviour matches the baseline. If the baseline gives no separate rule for a non-sending domain, keep the sending-domain check for every domain and say so, rather than inventing a rule.
- If a helper under `powershell/internal/` does the `SendingFromDomainDisabled` inference, give it a parameter for the list instead; do not read the setting in the helper.
- Update each test's `.md`, any unit tests under `powershell/tests/` that cover these tests, and `website/docs/configuration/` if it lists which tests use `ParkedDomains`. If parameters changed, regenerate `website/src/data/test-builder.json` with `./build/website/Update-MtTestBuilderData.ps1`.
- Do not touch `tests/cis/` (PR 2673 owns the CIS 2.1.8/2.1.9/2.1.10 tests), `powershell/assets/MaesterSettings.psd1`, or anything under `powershell/internal/engine/`: another session is editing those on `feat/parameter-settings`.

Done means: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` passes, the work is committed on your branch, pushed, and a PR is open against `feat/parameter-settings` (the base of PR 2758; say in the body that it is stacked on 2758 and changes results for tenants that relied on `SendingFromDomainDisabled`, and add the `breaking change` label). End the PR body with the line `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)` and commit messages with `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Report the PR link first.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/merill/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_338c3723-65a3-4813-9cbc-2a962282c882

## 2. Sender Policy Framework

The Sender Policy Framework (SPF) is a mechanism allowing domain
administrators to specify which IP addresses are explicitly approved to
send email on behalf of the domain, facilitating detection of spoofed
emails. SPF is not configured through the Exchange admin center, but
rather via Domain Name System (DNS) records hosted by the agency's
domain. The exact steps needed to set up SPF vary from agency to
agency. Microsoft's documentation provides some helpful starting
points.

### Policies

#### MS.EXO.2.2v3
An SPF policy SHALL be published for each domain that fails all non-approved senders.

[![BOD 25-01 Requirement](https://img.shields.io/badge/BOD_25--01_Requirement-C41230)](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/bod-25-01-implementation-guidance-implementing-secure-practices-cloud-services)
[![Automated Check](https://img.shields.io/badge/Automated_Check-5E9732)](#key-terminology)
[![Configurable](https://img.shields.io/badge/Configurable-005288)](../../../docs/configuration/parameters.md#preferreddnsresolvers)

<!--Policy: MS.EXO.2.2v3; Criticality: SHALL -->
- _Rationale:_ An adversary may modify email headers so the email appears to be a legitimate email sent by an
agency, facilitating phishing attacks. Publishing an SPF policy for each agency domain mitigates this by providing a means for recipients to detect emails spoofed in this way. SPF is required for FCEB agencies by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 18-01, "Enhance Email and Web Security."
- _Last modified:_ October 2025
- _Note:_ SPF defines two different "fail" mechanisms: fail (indicated by `-`, sometimes referred to as hardfail) and softfail (indicated by `~`). Either hardfail or softfail may be used to comply with this baseline policy.

#### MS.EXO.2.2v3 Instructions
First, identify any approved senders specific to your agency, e.g., any on-premises mail servers. SPF allows you to indicate approved senders by IP address or CIDR range. However, note that SPF allows you to [include](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208#section-5.2) the IP addresses indicated by a separate SPF policy, referred to by domain name. See [External DNS records required for SPF](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/external-domain-name-system-records?view=o365-worldwide#external-dns-records-required-for-spf) for inclusions required for M365 to send email on behalf of your domain.

SPF is not configured through the Exchange admin center but rather via
DNS records hosted by the agency's domain. The exact steps needed
to set up SPF varies from agency to agency. See [Add or edit an SPF TXT record to help prevent email spam (Outlook, Exchange Online) \| Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/get-help-with-domains/create-dns-records-at-any-dns-hosting-provider?view=o365-worldwide#add-or-edit-an-spf-txt-record-to-help-prevent-email-spam-outlook-exchange-online) for more details.

To test your SPF configuration, consider using a web-based tool, such as
those listed under [How can I validate SPF records for my domain? \| Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/setup/domains-faq?view=o365-worldwide#how-can-i-validate-spf-records-for-my-domain).
Additionally, SPF records can be requested using the
PowerShell tool `Resolve-DnsName`. For example:

```
Resolve-DnsName example.onmicrosoft.com txt
```

If SPF is configured, you will see a response resembling `v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all`
returned. The contents of the SPF
policy may vary by agency. In this example, the SPF policy indicates
the IP addresses listed by the policy for "spf.protection.outlook.com" are
the only approved senders for "example.onmicrosoft.com." These IPs can be determined
via an additional SPF lookup, this time for "spf.protection.outlook.com." Ensure the IP addresses listed as approved senders for your domain are correct. Additionally, ensure that each policy either ends in `-all` or `~all`, or [redirects](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208#section-6.1) to one that does. This directive indicates that all IPs that don't match the policy should fail. See [SPF TXT record syntax for Microsoft 365 \| Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/email-authentication-anti-spoofing?view=o365-worldwide#spf-txt-record-syntax-for-microsoft-365) for a more in-depth discussion
of SPF record syntax.

## 3. DomainKeys Identified Mail

DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) allows digital signatures to be added
to email messages in the message header, providing a layer of both
authenticity and integrity to emails. As with SPF, DKIM relies on DNS
records. The deployment of DKIM depends on how an agency manages its DNS.
Exchange Online Protection (EOP) features include DKIM signing capabilities.

### Policies

#### MS.EXO.3.1v1

## 4. Domain-Based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)
Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)
works with SPF and DKIM to authenticate mail senders and helps ensure
destination email systems can validate messages sent from your domain.
DMARC helps receiving mail systems determine what to do with messages
sent from your domain that fail SPF and DKIM checks.

### Policies

#### MS.EXO.4.1v1
A DMARC policy SHALL be published for every second-level domain.

[![BOD 25-01 Requirement](https://img.shields.io/badge/BOD_25--01_Requirement-C41230)](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/bod-25-01-implementation-guidance-implementing-secure-practices-cloud-services)

second-level domain protects the second-level domains and all subdomains.

### GlobalSettings

The `GlobalSettings` section contains organization-wide configuration that can be used by multiple tests. For example, you can define your emergency access accounts here so that all related tests use the same accounts.

A test receives a global setting as one of its parameters, so `Get-MtTest` shows which tests use it and the result shows the value each test ran with. To give one test a different value, set the parameter in that test's `TestSettings` row; it wins over `GlobalSettings`:

```json
{
  "GlobalSettings": { "ParkedDomains": ["contoso-old.com"] },
  "TestSettings": [ { "Id": "CIS.M365.2.1.9", "Parameters": { "ParkedDomains": [] } } ]
}
```

Stacked on #2758 (base `feat/parameter-settings`). Design: #2775.

The CISA Exchange email-authentication tests no longer decide which accepted domains are parked from Exchange's `SendingFromDomainDisabled`. A domain is parked only when it is listed in the shared `ParkedDomains` setting, which the engine binds to a test parameter. No test calls `Get-MtSetting`.

## Breaking change

Results change for tenants that relied on **Allow mail to be sent from this domain** being turned off:

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CISA.MS.EXO.2.2 (SPF) | A domain with sending disabled was left out of the test | It is checked as a sending domain (needs the Exchange Online include) unless it is listed in `ParkedDomains`. A listed domain must publish a policy ending in `-all` or `~all` |
| CISA.MS.EXO.3.1 (DKIM) | A domain with sending disabled was skipped as "Parked domain" | It is checked like every other domain and fails without an enabled DKIM configuration and a valid record |

To keep a parked domain passing 2.2, list it once:

```json
{ "GlobalSettings": { "ParkedDomains": ["contoso-old.com"] } }
```

## What SCuBA asks of a parked domain

Read from the ScubaGear baseline (`baselines/exo.md`), `EXOConfig.rego` and `ExportEXOProvider.psm1`. ScubaGear has no notion of a parked domain: it runs every policy against every accepted domain (the coexistence domain aside) and never reads `SendingFromDomainDisabled`.

| Policy | Baseline text | What a parked domain must publish | In this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MS.EXO.2.2v3 | An SPF policy for each domain "that fails all non-approved senders"; `-all` or `~all` both comply | An SPF policy ending in `-all` or `~all`. With no approved senders that is `v=spf1 -all` | Uses `ParkedDomains`. A listed domain is not asked for the Exchange Online include (Maester's check for a sending domain) and must fail all senders |
| MS.EXO.3.1v1 | DKIM "SHOULD be enabled for all domains" | No separate rule. Same as a sending domain | No parameter. The parked-domain skip is removed and every domain gets the sending-domain check |
| MS.EXO.4.1v1 | A DMARC policy for every second-level domain | No separate rule. A DMARC record | Unchanged; already checks every domain |
| MS.EXO.4.2v1 | `p=reject` | No separate rule. `p=reject` | Unchanged; already checks every domain |
| MS.EXO.4.3v1 | `rua` includes `reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov` | No separate rule | Unchanged |
| MS.EXO.4.4v1 (`Test-MtCisaDmarcReport`) | Agency contact in `rua` and `ruf` | No separate rule | Unchanged |

So only MS.EXO.2.2 takes `ParkedDomains`. The others keep the sending-domain check for every domain because the baseline gives no other rule.

**For the reviewer to rule on:** MS.EXO.3.1 now fails a parked domain that has no DKIM, where it used to skip it. That matches ScubaGear, but the alternative is to keep the skip for domains listed in `ParkedDomains`. I did not do that because the baseline has no such exemption.

## Changes

- `Test.CISA.MS.EXO.2.2.ps1`: `ParkedDomains` parameter bound to the setting; parked-domain rule; checks all accepted domains. Names are matched without regard to case or a trailing dot.
- `Test.CISA.MS.EXO.3.1.ps1`: removes the `SendingFromDomainDisabled` skip and the "Disable sending from domain" recommendation that depended on it.
- `Test.CISA.MS.EXO.4.2.ps1`, `Test.CISA.MS.EXO.4.3.ps1`, `Test-MtCisaDmarcReport.ps1`: the commented-out inference becomes a one-line comment. No behaviour change.
- Guides for 2.2 and 3.1 updated; 3.1 loses "Option 2: Disallow mail to be sent from domain".
- New `Test-MtCisaSpfDirective.Tests.ps1` (11 cases); `Test-MtDkim.Tests.ps1` expects a failure for the CISA parked case.

Not changed: `tests/cis/`, `MaesterSettings.psd1`, `powershell/internal/engine/`. `website/docs/configuration/` does not list tests per setting, and `Update-MtTestBuilderData.ps1` produced no diff.

## Notes

- #2673 also edits `powershell/tests/functions/Test-MtDkim.Tests.ps1` (the same parked case, for CIS), so whichever merges second has a small conflict there.
- The sending-domain rule in 2.2 is unchanged: it still asks for the Exchange Online include and does not check `-all`, which is narrower than MS.EXO.2.2v3. Left for a separate change.

## Testing

| MS.EXO.4.1, 4.2, 4.3 and the 4.4 helper | No separate rule | No behaviour change; they already checked every domain. Dead commented-out inference replaced by a comment. |

Decision for Merill: MS.EXO.3.1 now fails a parked domain without DKIM, where it used to skip it. That follows the brief's rule (no baseline exemption, so no invented one) and matches ScubaGear. The alternative is to skip domains listed in `ParkedDomains`; it is flagged in the PR body.

- **Unit tests:** added `Test-MtCisaSpfDirective.Tests.ps1` (11 cases) and changed the CISA parked case in `Test-MtDkim.Tests.ps1` to expect a failure. PR 2673 edits that same case, so whichever merges second gets a small conflict.

- **Docs and builder data:** `website/docs/configuration/` does not list tests per setting, so it is unchanged. `Update-MtTestBuilderData.ps1` produced no diff.
- **Left alone:** the sending-domain rule in 2.2 still only looks for the Exchange Online include and does not check `-all`, which is narrower than MS.EXO.2.2v3. Noted in the PR as a separate change.
